answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may post offers or vote on reputation. If several identities collude to endorse one another, a challenge period lets independent participants submit evidence of shared control; verified collusion burns their locked stake and removes the endorsements. This makes a sybil swarm costly rather than free: the attacker must tie up capital in every identity and risks losing it. A mesa of linked accounts may mirror one another’s praise, but a gale of cheap identities still cannot fake costly deposits.
